newsitem.title: JAPAN: Shin-Etsu to boost vinyl chloride output in U.S.
newsitem.headline: Shin-Etsu to boost vinyl chloride output in U.S.

text.p: Shin-Etsu Chemical Co Ltd said on Wednesday it would invest $700 million to boost its vinyl chloride production in the United States, and that it plans further expansion of its operations there.

A Shin-Etsu spokesman said the company's wholly owned U.S. unit had acquired a 15-square-kilometre site in Louisiana, and that the subsidiary would spend $700 million to build its second plant in the United States there.
The plant will begin operations in mid-1998, and will be capable of producing 500,000 tonnes of vinyl chloride resin and 500,000 tonnes of vinyl chloride monomer, he said.
Vinyl chloride resin is used for various household products and industrial goods.

The unit currently has a vinyl chloride plant in Texas and the new plant will bring Shin-Etsu Chemical's U.S. output of vinyl chloride resin to 1.75 million tonnes a year, the Shin-Etsu spokesman said.

"We are considering a further increase in output of vinyl chloride there. We may also produce other products we make (in Japan), but we have not specifically decided anything," the spokesman said. Shin-Etsu produces materials for electronics products as well.
